newsitem.title: USA: Philadelphia tax lien sale in doubt - paper.
newsitem.headline: Philadelphia tax lien sale in doubt - paper.

text.p: Approval for Philadelphia's planned tax lien sale is in doubt, with Mayor Ed Rendell aggressively lobbying city council members ahead of next week's vote, the Philadelphia Inquirer reported Friday.
Under the plan, the city would sell about 70,000 tax liens to a quasi-public agency, which would then hire private collection agencies to get overdue residents to pay late taxes.
The liens would be securitized with a roughly $100 million bond sale, and the proceeds would be divided between the city and the Philadelphia School District.
Some council members have expressed opposition to the plan, arguing that residents fallen on hard times would be harrassed by the private collection agencies.
